- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes or volatility; adjust downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >85), model overreacts with a steep upward trend that fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast slope by 10–15% after peak.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.2), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to sentiment magnitude.
- Mean reversion is strong in the 10–15 day window — if forecast is above 82.5, reduce by 0.5–1.0 per day until convergence to recent 10-day average.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after spike, model fails to anticipate — add a “drop buffer” rule: if last 3 days are rising >0.5% daily, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7 in next 3 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag by 2–4 days — adjust by adding 0.2–0.5 to forecast for days 1–3 if sentiment is neutral or negative.
